breakfast.name: Kashk-e Bademjan (Persian Eggplant Dip)
breakfast.description: Persian eggplant dip with caramelized onions and kashk (yogurt whey), served with lavash bread. A beloved Iranian breakfast and mezze dish with charred, smoky eggplant
instructions: Roast over open flame or in 400°F oven for 20-25 minutes until skin is charred and flesh is soft
Place roasted eggplants in bowl of cold water for 5 minutes until cool enough to handle
Peel away charred skin and discard, chop eggplant flesh coarsely
Heat oil in large pan and sauté sliced onion until golden (about 5 minutes)
Add minced garlic and turmeric, cook for 1 minute until fragrant
Add chopped eggplant and cook for 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally
Eggplant should break down into creamy consistency
Season with salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp dried mint
Garnish with fried onions and additional dried mint
Serve warm or at room temperature with lavash bread or pita for scooping
breakfast.notes: Kashk is Middle Eastern ingredient made from drained yogurt whey or sour milk. Can substitute with Greek yogurt mixed with lemon juice if kashk unavailable
breakfast.fun_fact: Kashk eggplant is a Persian eggplant dip traditionally served with bread like lavash, barbari, pita, or naan. Dried mint is important addition giving dish its distinctive flavor
